To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have engineered an Apolipoprotein-IL-15 chimeric protein that has improved pharmacokinetic properties and is able to be transferred to the liver and that it can be used to improve the immunological response of mice against a tumor model.

we constructed a novel IL-15 chimeric protein, APO-IL15, that is incorporated in part in the circulating HDL, and that liver gene transfer of APO- IL15 and IL-15 Rα Sushi plasmids enhances NK and memory CD8 lymphocyte expansion and has a modest therapeutic activity in mice against colon carcinoma.
the fusion of ApoA-I to IL-15 results in a chimeric protein with improved pharmacokinetics that can be incorporated into HDL, which is a promising strategy for immunotherapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a novel gene therapy for cancer that uses the liver as a factory to produce a fusion protein that becomes part of circulating high density lipoprotein particles.
the development of novel IL-15-based therapies that may be useful for the treatment of cancer.
the development of a gene therapy approach to treat cancer and other diseases using the APO-15 fusion protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the APO-hIL-15 construct was incorporated in part in HDL and that the construct showed improved biological activity when administered in combination with the Sushi domain of IL-2Rα.
the APO-15 fusion protein is a promising candidate for immunotherapy.
the Apo A-1 chimeric protein has a long plasma half-life and is incorporated in part into HDL.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an effective and safe method of gene transfer for the treatment of cancer.

we have developed a gene transfer approach that is able to deliver IL-15 to the liver, and that the protein is incorporated into circulating HDL, which is a very interesting finding that could be further exploited for the development of novel immunotherapeutic agents.
liver gene transfer of IL-15 constructs that become part of circulating HDL for immunotherapy is feasible.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Apo A-1 chimeric protein can be used for gene transfer to liver, and the fusion protein can be incorporated into HDL, and the combination of APO-APC and Sushi plasmids can be used to increase the bioactivity of the fusion protein.
liver gene transfer of APO-15 constructs is feasible, and can be used for immunotherapy.

liver gene transfer with plasmid constructs encoding APO-IL15 fusion protein and the sushi domain of the IL-15 receptor α subunit can be an effective strategy to increase the numbers of NK cells and memory T cells, with a potential application in cancer immunotherapy.
